citationText: “Integral Photography: A New Discovery by Professor Lippmann by the French Correspondent of the Scientific American.” Accessed: May 16, 2023. [Online]. Available: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/integral-photography/techniques can achieve a uniform resolution across the whole depth range. While early commercial light field displays are available, they have quite low spatial resolution and a limited depth of field. The images they produce have to be viewed “in a box” limited by their depth of field. This is an unacceptable constraint for the video industry and for other applications. The issue of depth of field must be resolved before light field displays can achieve wide acceptance. This article describes a way in which this can be done. Figure 20 shows the stark difference between the resolution generated by the conventional approach and through sharing ray angles across hogels and frames. Both traces in the figure are based on the same, “4K,” underlying display resolution. The example is based on a display resolution first introduced in the Sony Xperia Z5 Premium smartphone in 2015. The latest version of this smartphone has a 120-Hz frame rate, almost exactly in line with the example in this article. In the intervening years since the “4K” Xperia was first introduced, there have been substantial improvements
